draft_evidence.quote: “That thing looks fake,” Darius said. … “It looks like a lunchbox for rich people.”

findings.consequence: The repair still reads as a close paraphrase of the source rather than a genuinely fresh chapter. Beyond this exact opening construction, it preserves distinctive markers and sequence at draft/source lines 155/485 (“nineteen seconds”), 171/583 (three anonymous seconds after arrival), 289/869 (“West academic bridge”), 347/1085 (Elena's note), 365/1133 (“routing code”), 429/1295 (“operationally significant”), 515/1491 (“provisional…unresolved”), and 565/1633 (“wanted to stay”). A reader comparing editions will encounter substantially the same scene architecture, jokes, connective beats, and emotional landing.
findings.repair_target: Reconceive the chapter's dramatic route and interaction design while preserving locked facts and outcomes. Replace the source-derived airfield banter, flight acquaintance progression, orientation-map sequence, provisional-table structure, and closing realization with materially different staging, dialogue strategy, and connective causality—not sentence-level substitutions.

concerns: The final paragraphs restate the exit/staying meaning several times after the map, note, empty duffel, and phone call have already conveyed it; this is compression-oriented taste unless a later line-edit gate makes it contractual.
strengths: The emergency-map exercise gives Kade usable geography and makes departure a real, preserved option.
The revised fork confrontation gives Kade a clear evidence-versus-safety choice and lets the provisional students help without making them universal interpreters.
Class disparity is concrete through luggage, issued clothing, food accounting, and Kade's brief embarrassment.
The manuscript now meets the deterministic word-count limit, repairing verified finding F002.
Kade's attention to load paths, access permissions, costs, and exits strongly supports the selected voice.
